instruction: Switch VLC to minimal view to reduce interface clutter during my presentations.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling VLC's minimal view mode by setting qt-minimal-view=1 in the configuration (default is 0). The evaluator uses the existing check_qt_minimal_view metric function to verify the setting is enabled. The get_vlc_config getter reads the VLC config file (~/.config/vlc/vlcrc) and the metric checks if qt-minimal-view is set to 1. No new functions needed - reusing existing VLC evaluation infrastructure.
metadata.similarity_to_original: Very similar - both tasks involve changing a single VLC preference setting. Original disables splash cone (qt-bgcone=0), this enables minimal view (qt-minimal-view=1).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: enabling VLC minimal view mode
Getter logic (get_vlc_config) correctly extracts VLC configuration file from appropriate OS-specific location
Metric logic (check_qt_minimal_view) correctly parses config file and checks qt-minimal-view setting (default=0, expected=1)
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule' - directly accesses rule['expected_qt_minimal_view'] without incorrectly accessing rule['rules']
Expected value is semantically correct: qt-minimal-view=1 means enabled, matching instruction requirement
Postconfig appropriately kills and relaunches VLC to ensure config changes are applied before verification
Complete coverage: instruction has one requirement (enable minimal view), evaluator checks exactly that setting
Data flow is correct: VLC config file -> getter reads file -> metric checks specific setting -> comparison with expected value
